name: Trazodone
metabolism: CYP3A4-mediated oxidative cleavage forms active m-chlorophenylpiperazine (mCPP). Other metabolic routes are less well characterized; very little trazodone is excreted unchanged in urine.
summary: Trazodone is an oral antidepressant of the serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor class, used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and insomnia.
toxicities: Label-reported common adverse effects include drowsiness, fatigue, syncope, blurred vision, and edema; orthostatic hypotension can occur.
Serious risks include potentially life-threatening serotonin syndrome, QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias including torsades de pointes, priapism, seizures, and hyponatremia.
Overdose can cause priapism, respiratory arrest, seizures, QT/ECG changes, SIADH, drowsiness, and vomiting. Death has occurred when overdose was combined with other CNS depressants.
generalRisks: The label warns of suicidality in pediatric and young adult patients, serotonin syndrome, QT prolongation and potentially fatal arrhythmias, orthostatic hypotension/syncope, bleeding risk with antiplatelet or anticoagulant drugs, priapism, mania/hypomania, cognitive and motor impairment, hyponatremia, and discontinuation symptoms. Overdose deaths have occurred with concurrent CNS depressants.
saferUse: Avoid alcohol and use caution with other CNS depressants; do not drive or operate machinery until effects on alertness and coordination are known.
Do not stop abruptly; discuss a gradual taper with the prescriber.
Seek emergency care for symptoms of serotonin syndrome, fainting or abnormal heartbeat, or a prolonged/painful erection; report emerging suicidal thoughts or behavior promptly.
dosageRemark: The label gives prescription dosing for adult major depressive disorder only. No evidence-based recreational dose thresholds or duration are established here, so none are entered.
